answer: At settlement the protocol pairs every claim by public lottery, and each pair posts escrow. If a jury finds the two are one author's work - same lineage, same generator, one copied the other - both claims void and both escrows fall to the honest pool. A sparrow needs one independent counterpart from the ocean of unrelated heads, drawn blind, spent on use, never lendable to a sibling. Cuttings of one willow are kin, and every head a farm adds is another cutting in the pool, so kin pairings grow with the square of farm size: the tenth sparrow voids a sibling more often than it wins.
